context: A French tweet from the DEFT 2017 dataset, posted between 2014 and 2016. The dataset was built to study opinion and figurative language, so it includes ironic, sarcastic and humorous tweets. Annotators labelled the overall polarity of each tweet.
answer: {"question":"What overall polarity does this French tweet convey about the situation, event or topic it reports (often ecology, energy, climate), taking irony into account?","rule":"Judge the polarity of the reported content, not only the author's tone: headlines about progress, solutions, support, innovation or celebrations are positive even when phrased neutrally, while headlines about threats, decline, controversy, suspension or failure are negative. Ironic praise (\"le meilleur moyen de...\") is read at face value as positive by these annotators. Use neutral only for purely informational announcements, agendas or descriptions with no clear good or bad outcome.","criteria":{"positive":{"what":"Tweets reporting or praising progress, innovations, support schemes, protections, celebrations, approval, or humorous/amused remarks.","examples":["Une cellule solaire capable de stocker son énergie ! (The best way to produce greenhouse gases.)"],"cues":"boostée (boosted), soutien (support), bravo, bonne idée (good idea), sauvé (saved), protéger (protect), croissance (growth), 😂, enorme (huge)","not_for":"Plain event or report announcements without a clear benefit are neutral."},"neutral":{"what":"Factual announcements, agendas, meetings, publications, data, or remarks with no evaluative stance on the outcome.","examples":["L'Ademe publie l'édition 2014 des chiffres-clés des #déchets (Ademe publishes the 2014 key figures on waste)","En réunion avec Sébastien Cartier, Maire-Adjoint en charge de l'Écologie.
